Subject: Clarify audit-trigger clause / pen-test gating in order form

Irene — thanks again for the demo last week. As we start legal review on our side, a couple of contract items popped up that we need to resolve before procurement can move forward: 

1) Audit-trigger language: our counsel is concerned the proposed language lets the customer (HealthSync) trigger an on-site inspection beyond SOC 2 scope. Can you confirm the intended limits (assertions, sample sets, notice windows)?

2) Pen-test gating: the order form mentions a 72-hour notice for penetration testing but our security team expects a narrow staging window and an ability to require a signed NDA for tester access. Is that covered in Redwood's pen-test playbook?

If you can share a redline of the order form and a short note on the pen-test access flow we can move to procurement.

Appreciate quick turnaround — we have a board approval meeting next Thursday.

Tom Hale

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify audit-trigger clause / pen-test gating in order form

Tom — thanks for the note and the heads-up on your timeline. I pulled together a short redline and a proposed clarification we think will address HealthSync counsel's concern. Main points: 

- Audit-trigger: language we intend is limited to "reasonable inspection of written evidence and remediation artifacts related to SOC 2 assertions (CC) and supporting logs;" it does not grant unrestricted on-site access. We propose a 10-business-day notice for sampling runs and a sampler cap of 3% of total tenant activity for any customer-specific inspection.

- Pen-test gating: Redwood requires a 72-hour notice for simulated/organized testing on hosted environments, with a staging window option (we can provide a dedicated staging environment for tests). For on-production penetration testing we require:
  * A signed test-scoped NDA
  * Approved test plan (attacker IPs, schedule)
  * A maximum 4-hour live window unless otherwise agreed

I've attached: redlines_OrderForm_audit-trigger_v1.docx (redline of the order form) and pen-test-scope-matrix_v2.xlsx (mapping of recommended gating steps).

If that framing works, Karthik can review the exact order-form language for legal carve-outs (e.g., PII handling during sampling). Happy to jump on a 30m call if your counsel prefers to talk through.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Tom/Irene — quick legal read. Thanks for the redline, Irene — helpful. A few comments from counsel POV: 

- SOC 2 scope: we should be explicit that "SOC 2 attestation and related artifact access" is the default evidence set; customer-triggered inspections beyond SOC 2 assertions require executive approval and a scoped SOW. This gives us a path to say "no" to broad inspection asks while preserving cooperative audit requests.

- Sampling caps & notice: the 3% cap and 10-business-day notice are reasonable. Please confirm operationally that 3% is calculable and that your team can surface sample-set proof.

- Pen-test / NDA: standard. Suggest adding a sentence: "Redwood will provide a dedicated staging environment where feasible; for production testing Redwood reserves the right to decline tests that pose unacceptable risk to multi-tenant operations." Keeps our multi-tenant SLA protections intact.

I will prepare a short, clean paragraph we can insert into the order form (no redline doc for this — I'll paste the language in my next mail). Priyom, inventory please: are there any evidence types (logs, retained traces) we cannot provide that we should call out?
